scenes.heading: Data Lifecycle
scenes.subheading: From creation to archival and everything between
scenes.narration: The data lifecycle describes the stages data passes through, from the moment it is generated to when it is finally archived or deleted.

scenes.heading: Stages of the lifecycle
bullets: Storage in a durable, queryable form
Processing and transformation into usable data
Archival or deletion when no longer needed
scenes.narration: Data is first generated by a source such as an app or sensor. It is ingested into a central platform where it can be managed. It is stored durably so it can be queried later. It is processed and transformed into a usable shape. It is served to analysts and applications that create value, and eventually it is archived or deleted once its usefulness has passed.

scenes.heading: The lifecycle in motion
scenes.narration: Each stage flows naturally into the next, beginning with generation and ingestion. Data is then stored, processed, and served for real use. When its value declines, it is archived or removed to control cost and risk.

scenes.text: Understanding the data lifecycle helps engineers manage cost, quality, and governance at every stage.
scenes.narration: Thinking in terms of a lifecycle helps engineers make deliberate choices about cost, quality, and governance at each stage of a dataset's existence.
